revisions.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Production asset for BRINE, a top-down underwater industrial pixel-art station builder. Carefully rendered chunky pixel-art forms with selective fine detail, muted deep-ocean palette, soft upper-left ambient light, no sunlight beams. Orthographic overhead camera, no horizon, no isometric diamond. No text, labels, UI, border, station structures, characters, bright glow or fantasy crystals. One individual reusable scenery sprite: one low irregular cluster of three pale grey-ochre anhydrite mineral chimneys and porous sulfur-coated nodules, squat broken tubes with dark mouths, no smoke or bubbles, no lava. Matching habitat: Sulfur vent basin. Entire silhouette visible, centered with generous empty exterior margin. TRUE TRANSPARENT BACKGROUND with actual alpha=0 outside the subject, never draw checkerboard or a colored backdrop. No broad ground disk, no scenery outside this isolated cluster, no cast shadow beyond its tiny contact base. Readable at small gameplay scale. Square canvas. CRITICAL CAMERA AND SHAPE OVERRIDE: camera directly above looking straight down, 85 to 90 degree overhead. Everything is very LOW AND SQUAT, pancake-like in height. Show predominantly TOP surfaces. Tube mouths are nearly circular rings with just a tiny rim of south-facing wall, NOT tall cylinders. Sea-fan branches spread horizontally close to the seafloor, like a broad flattened coral rosette seen directly from above; NOT an upright frontal fan. The top-view horizontal footprint dominates. No three-quarter portrait view, no tall front walls, no tall central tower, no isometric arrangement. Authentic transparent outer canvas.
revisions.reason: v1 is too upright/front-facing for seabed placement
